llm.summary: This skill is a small, disclosed guide for using the QName CLI for one-domain WHOIS and availability lookups.

dimensions.detail: Terminal and network use are proportionate to a domain lookup integration, and the skill gives a clear one-domain-per-command limit.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact does not ship executable code or an installer, but it instructs users to configure the existing CLI with an approved API key through qname-cli init or an environment variable.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime guidance is limited to qname-cli commands, JSON/text output choices, credential debugging, and direct HTTP calls only for API contract validation or CLI debugging.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: qname-cli init may persist an API key in local config, but this is disclosed and the skill recommends environment variables for ephemeral agent sessions; no background workers, hooks, privilege escalation, or hidden persistence are present.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is narrow: invoke qname-cli for single-domain WHOIS/domain availability evidence via QName.AI, with batch lookups, traffic data, rating data, streaming checks, and purchase actions explicitly out of scope.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, make sure you trust QName.AI with the domains you query and protect the QName API key like any other secret. Prefer the environment-variable setup for temporary agent sessions, and only use persistent qname-cli init when you are comfortable storing the key locally.
